reuse.why: The new handler reuses recurConfigToRSchedule and applyWeekendRule, while existing consumers receive the extended policy through the same helpers.

duplication.why: Holiday matching and nonworking-day decisions are centralized rather than copied into individual consumers.

placement.why: Calendar policy remains in shared/schedules.ts, configuration belongs in the schedule model, and endpoint orchestration stays in the schedules server app.

scope.why: The edits address the four requested schedule changes and their affected consumers, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared policy is straightforward, although separate hard-coded occurrence-search limits in getNextDate and getUpcomingDates create maintenance coupling as exclusion rules evolve.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All changed consumers apply the calendar policy through applyWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: Weekend and holiday policy is shared explicitly, with no renamed or reshaped duplicate implementation.

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule gains frequency and holidays inputs plus a daily-frequency branch; getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter, with all consumers retaining the shared policy.
